subject: accountancy
chapter_title: Graphs and Charts for Business Data

concepts.title: Graphs and Charts: Meaning and Business Uses
concepts.definition: A graph is a pictorial presentation of data carrying at least a two-dimensional relationship, drawn on a horizontal X-axis and a vertical Y-axis; it may be single-line or multiple-line, with distinct line styles and colours separating the lines. Charts turn a mass of raw figures into a picture that communicates accounting information faster than tables -- a picture being worth more than a thousand words.
concepts.key_idea: Raw figures hide their message; a two-axis picture delivers it at a glance.
question_patterns: define charts and graphs and explain how they are useful in business decisions
why is a graph called a pictorial representation with at least two dimensions
how do multiple lines in one graph stay distinguishable from each other

solution_steps.explain: pictorial presentation of data on X and Y axes, single-line or multiple-line
charts communicate accounting information quickly where raw data resist understanding

concepts.title: Quarter-wise Sales Totals for Charting
concepts.definition: Before charting, the worksheet totals the data: row totals give quarter-wise sales of all products and column totals give product-wise sales, with the corner cell holding the overall total. For the sample year 2007-08 of ABC Manufacturing Company, the four quarterly totals add up to the annual sales figure that the chart then displays period-wise.
concepts.key_idea: Add the four quarterly totals to get the annual sales figure the chart will show period-wise.
question_patterns: add the Qtr1 to Qtr4 quarterly sales 25844, 11295, 14744 and 21886 to get the annual total plotted in the graph
the row totals of quarterly sales in the worksheet combine into which annual total for the period-wise graph
find the annual total sales that the quarter-wise graph of ABC Manufacturing displays
compute the year total from four quarterly figures before plotting the sales graph
which sum of the four quarters equals the annual total sales shown in the graph

solution_steps.explain: the annual sales figure is the sum of the quarter-wise totals of all products

concepts.title: Pie Chart Percentage Share
concepts.section: 4.2.3 Change the Chart Type: pie share
concepts.definition: In a pie chart every slice shows the size of one item proportionately, and all slices together equal 100 per cent of the whole. A slice's percentage is its value divided by the total of all values, multiplied by 100 -- the same arithmetic the software applies when it labels the parts of the pie.
concepts.key_idea: Divide the part by the whole and multiply by 100 -- the slices must always sum to 100 per cent.
concepts.textbook_ref: leca104.txt, pie chart percentage and steps (approx lines 379-436)
question_patterns: the second quarter sold 11295 against an annual total of 73769; find its percentage share of the pie
a quarter contributing 14744 to total sales of 73769 holds what percentage of the pie chart
compute the slice percentage when a category's value and the whole total are known
why must all the slices of a pie chart together equal 100 per cent
two-wheelers number 23456 of 52095 vehicles registered; what percentage slice do they form

solution_steps.action: divide the part by the whole
solution_steps.explain: the slice's fraction of the whole, scaled by 100, gives its percentage of the pie

concepts.title: Product Series Totals for Radar Comparison
concepts.definition: A radar chart compares the aggregate values of several data series without any category axis. For the personal-care products table, each series -- lowest sales and highest sales -- totals across six products: toothpaste, toothbrush, hair oil, shampoo, toilet soap and bath soap; the two totals then anchor the comparison the radar chart draws.
concepts.formula: series_total = p1_value + p2_value + p3_value + p4_value + p5_value + p6_value
concepts.key_idea: Total each data series across all products before the radar chart compares the aggregates.
concepts.textbook_ref: leca104.txt, product lowest-highest table and radar chart (approx lines 532-578)
question_patterns: the lowest sales are 2345, 500, 988, 2900, 1122 and 952 across six products; find the series total
add the highest sales 12344, 5415, 3678, 3770, 3861 and 2344 to get the aggregate
compute the aggregate of a data series before plotting it on a radar chart
what distinguishes a radar chart from charts built on category axes
find the combined lowest-sales figure of the six personal-care products

solution_steps.explain: each data series aggregates across the products to give one comparable figure
solution_steps.compute: series_total = p1_value + p2_value + p3_value + p4_value + p5_value + p6_value

concepts.title: Vehicle Registration Total for the RTO Pie Chart
concepts.definition: A pie chart of vehicles registered in a city during 2007-08 needs the registration total first: buses, trucks, auto-rickshas, cars, two-wheelers and heavy vehicles each contribute their count, and the six counts add to the whole that the pie divides into percentage slices.
concepts.formula: registered_total = bus_count + truck_count + auto_count + car_count + two_wheeler_count + heavy_count
concepts.key_idea: The pie can only divide a whole, so total all vehicle types before slicing.
concepts.textbook_ref: leca104.txt, Skill Review F vehicle table (approx lines 883-901)
question_patterns: vehicles registered are 575 buses, 5889 trucks, 12345 autos, 9765 cars, 23456 two-wheelers and 65 heavy vehicles; find the total registered

solution_steps.explain: the registration whole equals the sum of every vehicle type's count
solution_steps.compute: registered_total = bus_count + truck_count + auto_count + car_count + two_wheeler_count + heavy_count

concepts.title: Marks Distribution Total and Column Chart Share
concepts.definition: A column chart of students' marks bands first totals the distribution: the five class intervals from 0-20 to 81-100 together hold all the students examined. Each band's share of that total shows how the class spread across the intervals, the comparison the column chart draws bar by bar.
concepts.formula: students_total = band1_count + band2_count + band3_count + band4_count + band5_count
concepts.key_idea: Sum the marks bands to the full cohort, then the columns compare each band's count.
concepts.textbook_ref: leca104.txt, Skill Review G marks table (approx lines 903-919)
question_patterns: the marks bands hold 113, 180, 350, 232 and 125 students; find the total number of students
compute the cohort size from the five class intervals of the marks distribution
add the band counts 113, 180, 350, 232 and 125 before drawing the column chart
what does each column of the marks chart represent once the total is known
verify that the five interval counts of 1000 students add back to the total

solution_steps.explain: the five class intervals together cover every student in the cohort
solution_steps.compute: students_total = band1_count + band2_count + band3_count + band4_count + band5_count

concepts.title: Elements of a Chart
concepts.definition: Every chart carries named elements: the chart area covering the entire chart; the plot area bounded by the axes in 2-D and by three axes in 3-D; data points plotted as bars, columns, lines or pie slices, where same-coloured markers form a data series; the horizontal category axis carrying independent values and the vertical value axis carrying dependent values; the legend identifying each series by colour or pattern; chart and axis titles; and data labels that spell out a marker's details.
concepts.formula: chart_parts = chart_area plus plot_area plus data_series plus axes plus legend plus titles plus labels
concepts.key_idea: From the outer chart area to the smallest data label, each named element plays one role in reading the picture.
question_patterns: describe the elements of a chart: chart area, plot area, data series and legend
what is the difference between the chart area and the plot area
what do data markers of the same colour together constitute
which axis carries categories and which carries dependent values
what extra information does a data label provide for a data point

solution_steps.explain: chart area wraps everything; plot area holds the plotting between the axes
data points form series, the legend identifies them, titles describe them and labels annotate them

concepts.title: Choosing Chart Types: Pie, Column, Line, Doughnut and Radar
concepts.definition: Each chart type answers a different question. A pie chart shows the relative share of parts in one whole; a column or bar chart compares absolute values of items or time periods; a line chart traces changes over time; a doughnut chart relates parts to a whole across more than one series, each ring one series, though it reads poorly and a stacked column often serves better; a radar chart compares aggregate values of several series without category axes.
concepts.formula: chart_choice = pie for share plus column for comparison plus line for trends
concepts.key_idea: Shares go to pie, comparisons to columns, trends to lines, multi-series wholes to doughnuts.
concepts.textbook_ref: leca104.txt, chart type descriptions and summary (approx lines 17-29, 561-615, 642-688)
question_patterns: differentiate between pie charts, line charts and column charts
which chart type best shows the trend of data over a period

which chart suits comparing sales of products at discrete time intervals

solution_steps.explain: pie for relative share, column or bar for comparing absolute values, line for movement over time
doughnut carries multiple rings of series, radar compares aggregates with no category axis

concepts.title: Conditions for a Pie Chart
concepts.definition: Excel can turn a column or bar chart into a pie in a few clicks, but the data must qualify: only one data series is plotted, the plotted values are positive, and no value equals zero. Also, a pie cannot carry more than seven categories, because the categories are the parts of the whole pie.
concepts.formula: pie_rules = one_series plus positive_values plus at most seven_categories
concepts.key_idea: One positive series and at most seven categories -- otherwise the pie misrepresents the whole.
concepts.textbook_ref: leca104.txt, pie chart conditions and creation steps (approx lines 399-436)
question_patterns: a pie chart does not accept more than how many categories

solution_steps.explain: one series, strictly positive values, and no more than seven categories qualify for a pie
select the chart, choose pie and its sub-type such as 3-D pie from the ribbon tools

concepts.title: 2-D and 3-D Charts and Their Axes
concepts.definition: A 2-D chart plots on two axes: the horizontal category axis takes the independent known values -- months, quarters, products -- and the vertical value axis takes the dependent derived values. Negative values fall on the far side of the origin, so profit and loss plot above and below the axis. A 3-D chart adds the depth or series axis, the Z-axis, plotting along the depth -- as representing volume needs height, length and breadth together.
concepts.formula: chart_axes = category_x plus value_y plus depth_z in three dimensions
concepts.key_idea: X carries categories, Y carries values, and only 3-D adds the Z depth axis.
question_patterns: differentiate between 2-D charts and 3-D charts

in plotting monthly demand, what goes on the X-axis and what on the Y-axis

solution_steps.explain: categories on the horizontal X, derived values on the vertical Y, negatives beyond the origin
the Z or depth axis lets data plot along the depth of a 3-D chart

concepts.title: Formatting Charts with Design, Layout and Format
concepts.definition: Clicking a chart raises the Chart Tools with three tabs. Design changes chart type, layouts and styles, and its Switch Row/Column swaps the plotted data between axes. Format handles the selected element's look: shape fill with colours, pictures, gradients or textures, outline colour, weight and dashes, effects like shadow and bevel, and WordArt text styles. Layout inserts pictures, clip art, data labels and gridlines.
concepts.formula: format_tabs = design plus layout plus format
concepts.key_idea: Design restyles the whole chart, Layout adds insertions, Format dresses the selected element.
question_patterns: which three options do the chart tools provide for formatting a chart
what does the switch row or column option do to a plotted chart
which formatting choices exist under shape fill for a chart element
how is the weight or thickness of a chart line or border changed
what does the legend allow once a chart carries multiple series

solution_steps.explain: Design for type, layout and style; Layout for insertions; Format for the element's fill, outline, effects and text
Switch Row/Column exchanges what plays on the X-axis and the Y-axis

concepts.title: Steps to Create, Resize and Move a Chart
concepts.definition: Chart-making follows a fixed order: enter data with proper row and column titles; create the basic chart from the chart groups on the ribbon; change its layout or style; add or remove chart titles, axis titles and data labels; show or hide the legend; display or hide axes and gridlines; move or resize the chart -- dragging its borders with the two-headed arrow cursor; and finally save it. Excel redraws the chart automatically whenever the underlying data or range changes.
concepts.formula: chart_steps = enter_data plus insert_type plus style plus labels plus legend plus move_resize plus save
concepts.key_idea: Data first, chart type next, then dress it with titles, legend and gridlines, resize, and save.
concepts.textbook_ref: leca104.txt, chart steps in summary and section 4.2.4 (approx lines 693-722, 467-475)
question_patterns: describe the steps to move, resize and reposition a chart
which steps prepare a chart from worksheet data in Excel

solution_steps.explain: enter titled data, insert the chart type, then style, label, legend and gridlines
drag borders to resize, reposition as needed, and save; edits to data redraw the chart automatically

concepts.title: Advantages of Graphs: Explore, Present, Convince
concepts.definition: Graphs serve three purposes. They help explore -- testing whether variables relate, say a country's GNP and infant mortality, is quicker on a chart than paging through raw data. They help present -- conveying information in the least time, as newspapers and newsmagazines understood early. And they help convince -- distilling large amounts of information into displays that persuade, and exposing trends even in highly random data such as stock prices.
concepts.formula: graph_purpose = explore plus present plus convince
concepts.key_idea: Charts explore relationships, present them fastest, and convince an audience of them.
question_patterns: state the three advantages of using graphs and charts for business data
how do graphs help in exploring a relationship between two variables
why do newspapers and magazines rely on charts to sum up their articles
how can a chart convince an audience where a table of numbers fails
why do graphs suit highly random data such as stock price movements

solution_steps.explain: explore relationships quickly, present information in little time, convince with distilled displays
even random series like stock prices yield their fluctuations to a visual treatment
